observation_summary: A unit test (BrentOptimizerTest::testKeepInitIfBest) fails with "Best point not reported": the optimizer's returned point (sol) has a larger objective value than an earlier point (expected == init). The bug report states BrentOptimizer does not check that the point it will return is the best one it has encountered.
reasoning_summary: The failure and the bug description indicate the optimizer is missing a validation/guard that compares the candidate return point against the best-evaluated point and selects the better one. This is a missing/incorrect predicate check (ensure returned point is best), so the root cause is a missing conditional/validation rather than a simple wrong assignment, concurrency issue, API mismatch, or a broader design-level capability gap.
evidence_used: Assert.assertTrue("Best point not reported", f.value(sol) <= f.value(expected)); (BrentOptimizerTest.java:221)
Failing test: org.apache.commons.math3.optimization.univariate.BrentOptimizerTest::testKeepInitIfBest -> junit.framework.AssertionFailedError: Best point not reported

bug_report_description: "BrentOptimizer does not check that the point it is going to return is indeed the best one it has encountered. Indeed, the last evaluated point might be slightly worse than the one before last."
evidence_gaps: No pre-fix implementation snippet of BrentOptimizer's return logic provided (can't point to exact missing if/compare line).
No failing run-time values showing numeric difference between sol and expected beyond the assertion message.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: Although the symptom arises from the algorithm returning the last evaluated point, the explicit bug description and test indicate the fix is to add a check/select best-before-returning (a missing validation) rather than a wholesale rewrite of the algorithm's core procedure.
There is no evidence of an incorrect assigned constant or wrong initialization; the issue is choosing the wrong candidate due to missing verification, not an incorrect variable/value initialization.
The functionality (optimizer) exists and runs; the bug is not an unimplemented capability or missing class but a missing check in existing logic.
No boundary or API/parameter mismatch is indicated; failure is internal to the optimizer's decision logic.
No concurrency, ordering, or locking concerns are described; this is not a serialization/timing issue.
No evidence of inconsistency among related structures or components; the problem is a missing validation step within a single component.
